_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Oil Analysis Report
summary: The Oil Analysis Report provides technical information required to support the maintenance of engines, transmissions, and other lubricated components, used to improve operational readiness and detect impending component failures.
description_purpose:
The Oil Analysis Report provides technical information required to support the maintenance of engines, transmissions, and other components (i.e., hydraulic, final drives) that utilize lubricating oil to reduce friction or wear.
Reports are used to improve operational readiness, promote safety, detect impending component failures and conserve resources by applying on-condition oil changes.
application_interrelationship:
This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format and content preparation instructions for the data product generated by the specific and discrete task requirement as delineated in the contract.
This Data Item Description should be incorporated into development contracts for equipment anticipated to require the use of lubricating oil(s).
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Format.
preparation_instructions.content: The Oil Analysis Report shall be in the contractor's format. When the contract requires multiple or revised submissions of the Oil Analysis Report, each submission shall retain the format initially utilized.

preparation_instructions.title: Content.
preparation_instructions.content: The Oil Analysis Report shall consist of the following information:

children.title: Oil analysis wearmetal signatures or developed guidelines in parts per million (PPM).
Identification of normal and abnormal wearlevels in parts per million (PPM) as developed using standard analytical instruments compatible with those used by the Army.
Acceptable break-in wearmetal levels and length of time required for acceptable break-in of item.
Description and metallurgy of all moving parts subject to wear and lubricated by the lubricating oil system with identification of critical parts.
Component and assembly cutaway drawings or sketches which clearly identify critical elements subject to wear.
Locations of sampling valves for obtaining used oil samples for oil analysis.
The integrity of the used oil sample and the accessibility of the oil sampling valve.
Chemical composition of lubricants that are other than standard specification lubricants.
List of oil lubricated components (e.g., transmissions, engines, axles, fluid and hydraulic drives) in descending order of failure rates.
Lubricant physical property limitations (e.g., normal viscosity range, levels of contamination).
